summary: Fortune reviews the Delta SkyMiles Gold Business American Express Card, aimed at small business owners who fly Delta often. It offers a 75,000-mile welcome bonus, a free first checked bag, priority boarding and a 15% Takeoff15 discount on award flights, with a $0 intro annual fee for the first year (then $99). Downsides are no lounge access and modest rewards rates. The review compares it with the Chase Ink Business Preferred card for more flexible rewards.
one_line: Fortune reviews the Delta SkyMiles Gold Business Amex, a $99 airline card for frequent Delta flyers with a 75,000-mile bonus and bag perks.
key_facts: The Delta SkyMiles Gold Business American Express Card offers 75,000 Bonus Miles after $6,000 in purchases in the first 6 months.
The annual fee is $0 intro for the first year, then $99; there is no foreign transaction fee.
Rewards are 2x miles on Delta purchases, U.S. advertising in select media, U.S. shipping and restaurant dining, and 1x on other eligible purchases.
The card does not provide access to Delta Sky Club or Delta's airport lounges.
Cardholders and up to nine guests get the first checked bag free; the standard bag fee is $30, so using it more than three times beats the annual fee.
Takeoff15 gives a 15% discount when booking Delta and Delta Connection flights with miles through the Fly Delta app or Delta SkyMiles account.
Spending $10,000 or more in eligible purchases in a year earns a $100 Delta eCredit.
Cardholders get 20% back as a statement credit on eligible in-flight purchases such as meals, alcohol and audio headsets on Delta flights.
Other benefits include priority boarding for up to nine guests, baggage insurance, and car rental loss and damage insurance.
The Chase Ink Business Preferred Credit Card has a $95 annual fee and a 100,000-point bonus after $8,000 spent in the first three months.

Ink Business Preferred pays 3x points on up to $150,000 combined in shipping, internet, cable, phone and social media/search engine advertising, and points transfer 1:1 to Virgin Atlantic or Flying Blue.
Applicants should aim for a good FICO score of 690 or better.
Recent Delta SkyMiles Award Deals from Seattle included Chicago (ORD) for 8,000 miles and Auckland (AKL) for 64,000 miles one way in economy.
